newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bank floats more bonds to curb liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Thai bank floats more bonds to curb liquidity.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday it sharply raised its March 21, one-month weekly bond auction to 20 billion baht from a previously planned two billion in order to curb expected excess liquidity later this month.

A central bank statement said the decision was a pre-emptive move against anticipated higher liquidity in the banking system after a scheduled withdrawal of about 70-80 billion baht of start-up funds by the Government Pension Fund on March 27.

The statement said the central bank may also increase the size of other bond issues to be auctioned in the next few weeks to ensure that adjustment of domestic interest rates proceeds in an orderly fashion.

Analysts said the central bank move was consistent with its earlier policy of maintaining relatively high Thai interest rates to discourage outflows of baht funds used for speculating on the U.S. dollar.
But they said the bank policy appeared to run against broader government efforts to bring down domestic lending rates in order to ease business funding costs and spur a sluggish Thai economy.
Thai prime bank lending rates have stood at 13.25-13.75 percent since early 1995, among the highest in the region.
The Thai baht faced sporadic market attacks in December and February by speculators who bet that Thailand may be forced to devalue the currency later this year to boost weak exports.
The central bank has ruled out any devaluation plan and it has intervened in both local and foreign markets to defend the baht.
